'''Loyal Durand''' (also known as L. Durand III or Randy Durand) is an American theoretical physicist and Professor Emeritus of Physics at the [[University of Wisconsin-Madison]]. He is recognized for his contributions to high-energy particle physics, especially phenomenological models of scattering and applications of [[Quantum chromodynamics|QCD]], contributions to [[special functions]] and mathematical physics, and work at the [[Aspen Center for Physics]].<ref name="AspenBio">{{cite web |url=https://aspenphys.org/people/loyal-randy-durand/ |title=Loyal (Randy) Durand |website=Aspen Center for Physics |access-date=June 30, 2026}}</ref><ref name="PresEssay">{{cite web |url=https://aspenphys.org/presidential-essay-from-randy-durand/ |title=Presidential Essay from Randy Durand |website=Aspen Center for Physics |access-date=June 30, 2026}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Loyal Durand earned his B.S. in Physics from [[Yale University]] in 1953.<ref name="AspenBio" /> He then remained at Yale for graduate studies and completed his Ph.D. in 1957 under [[Gregory Breit]]. His thesis examined vacuum polarization effects in proton-proton scattering.<ref name="YaleProfile">{{cite web |url=https://physics.yale.edu/people/loyal-durand |title=Loyal Durand |website=Yale University Department of Physics |access-date=June 30, 2026}}</ref>

==Career==
After completing his doctorate, Durand held postdoctoral appointments at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] (1957-1959) and [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] (1959-1961). He joined the Yale faculty in 1961 and remained there until 1965, when he moved to the [[University of Wisconsin-Madison]] as a full professor of physics, a position he held until his retirement as Professor Emeritus.<ref name="AspenBio" /><ref name="YaleProfile" /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.physics.wisc.edu/directory/durand-loyal/ |title=Loyal Durand |website=University of Wisconsin-Madison Department of Physics |access-date=June 30, 2026}}</ref> He has held visiting or staff positions at (or served on advisory committees for) major national laboratories including [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]], [[Argonne National Laboratory]], [[Fermilab]], and [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]].<ref name="UWNewsletter">{{cite web |url=https://www.physics.wisc.edu/newsletter/news00.pdf |title=The Wisconsin Physicist, Vol. 7, No. 1 (Winter 2000–2001) |publisher=University of Wisconsin–Madison Department of Physics |access-date=July 17, 2026}}</ref>

Durand’s association with the [[Aspen Center for Physics]] began in 1962 and continued for more than six decades. He served as Chair of the Executive Committee (1968-1972), President (1972-1976), Trustee (1968-1980), and has been an Honorary Trustee since 1980. In addition to these organizational roles, he helped in documenting the Center’s history through essays and oral history interviews that preserve the early development of theoretical physics programs at the institution.<ref name="AspenBio" /><ref name="PresEssay" /> He has lived full-time in Aspen since 2011.<ref name="AspenBio" />

==Research==
Durand’s research has been on theoretical particle physics.<ref name="AspenBio" />

An early contribution was his 1962 calculation of pionic (hadronic) contributions to the [[Muon g-2|anomalous magnetic moment of the muon]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Durand |first1=L. |title=Pionic contributions to the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon |journal=[[Physical Review]] |volume=128 |pages=441-448 |year=1962}}</ref>

An early paper in high-energy phenomenology was his 1968 collaboration with R. Lipes on a diffraction model for high-energy proton-proton scattering.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Durand III |first1=L. |last2=Lipes |first2=R. |title=Diffraction Model for High-Energy pp Scattering |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] |volume=20 |issue=12 |pages=637-640 |year=1968 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.20.637}}</ref>

Representative of his work on special functions is the 1976 paper with P. M. Fishbane and L. M. Simmons, Jr., on expansion formulas and addition theorems for [[Gegenbauer polynomials|Gegenbauer functions]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Durand |first1=L. |last2=Fishbane |first2=P. M. |last3=Simmons, Jr. |first3=L. M. |title=Expansion formulas and addition theorems for Gegenbauer functions |journal=[[Journal of Mathematical Physics]] |volume=17 |issue=11 |pages=1933-1948 |year=1976}}</ref>

In later work he explored semihard QCD effects, the relationship between virtual and real scattering cross sections, and other topics that extended into publications through the 2010s.<ref name="AspenBio" /> Durand frequently collaborated with his wife, physicist [[Bernice Durand]], on topics including duality in heavy-quark systems.<ref name="Pubs">{{cite web |url=https://pages.hep.wisc.edu/~ldurand/Vitae/publications.html |title=Publications |website=Prof. L. Durand's Home Page |access-date=June 30, 2026}}</ref>

==Honors and leadership==
Durand was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1971.<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Fellows archive |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>

His long-term leadership at the [[Aspen Center for Physics]], combined with his efforts to document its institutional history, has been acknowledged within the theoretical physics community.<ref name="AspenBio" /><ref name="PresEssay" />

==Personal life==
Durand was married to Wesley Ann Travis from 1954 to 1966. One of their sons is [[Chris Durand|Christopher A. Durand]], a stuntman, actor, and writer (professionally known as Chris Durand).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.aspentimes.com/obituaries/wesley-ann-norton/ |title=Wesley Ann Norton obituary |website=Aspen Times |access-date=June 30, 2026}}</ref>

In October 1970 he married physicist Bernice Durand (née Black). The couple collaborated on multiple research papers and jointly endowed undergraduate research scholarships in physics and astronomy at the University of Wisconsin and Iowa State University. Bernice Durand died in February 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/madison/name/bernice-durand-obituary?id=33181552 |title=Bernice Durand Obituary |website=Legacy.com |date=February 22, 2022 |access-date=June 30, 2026}}</ref>
